instructions: Cut the chorizo into 3/4-inch slices. Slice the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the garlic for 2 minutes, until soft and pale yellow.
Add the chorizo and cook for 4 minutes, until it starts to brown.

Pour in the cider, then add the pepper and bay leaves. Turn the heat down and simmer for 12 minutes, until the cider has reduced to a thick, slightly syrupy sauce and the chorizo is cooked through to 160°F, or has no raw pink in the middle.
Take the pan off the heat and remove the bay leaves. Stir in the parsley and serve with the gluten-free bread.
method_notes: Food Drink Destinations (4.8 from 4 reviews) was the one version read with amounts, so it leads as a fallback; the bay leaves come from Fascinating Spain's version, which simmers the chorizo in cider with nothing else. Both agree on cooking the sausage in apple cider until it reduces to a little sauce, and they differ on whether to brown the sausage first (this follows the lead). The amounts are doubled from the lead's 1/2 lb tapa portion for a dinner. The bread is gluten-free to keep the dish gluten-free; check the chorizo and cider labels too.
